void TestNewShaderRecompilerUnsupportedMemoryDecode() {
  const uint32_t mubuf_unknown[] = {EncodeMubuf0(0x7b), EncodeMubuf1(0, 0, 1),
                                    0xbf810000u};
  CheckNewDecoderUnsupported(mubuf_unknown,
                             static_cast<uint32_t>(std::size(mubuf_unknown)),
                             "MUBUF", "opcode=0x7b");

  const uint32_t flat_unknown[] = {EncodeFlat0(0x7e, 0, 4),
                                   EncodeFlat1(9, 0x7d, 0, 1), 0xbf810000u};
  CheckNewDecoderUnsupported(flat_unknown,
                             static_cast<uint32_t>(std::size(flat_unknown)),
                             "FLAT", "opcode=0x7e");

  const uint32_t mtbuf_unknown[] = {EncodeMtbuf0(0x08, 14, 7, 4),
                                    EncodeMtbuf1(0x08, 9, 0, 1), 0xbf810000u};
  CheckNewDecoderUnsupported(mtbuf_unknown,
                             static_cast<uint32_t>(std::size(mtbuf_unknown)),
                             "MTBUF", "opcode=0x08");

  const uint32_t bpermute_gds[] = {
      EncodeDs0(0xb3) | (1u << 17u), EncodeDs1(1, 3, 17), 0xbf810000u};
  CheckNewDecoderUnsupported(bpermute_gds,
                             static_cast<uint32_t>(std::size(bpermute_gds)),
                             "DS", "available only for LDS");
}

void TestNewShaderRecompilerFlatUserPointerUsesDma() {
  const uint32_t shader[] = {
      EncodeVop2(0x25, 0, 0, 2), // v_add_nc_u32 v0, s0, v2
      EncodeVop1(0x01, 1, 1),    // v_mov_b32 v1, s1
      EncodeFlat0(0x0c, 0, 0),
      EncodeFlat1(3, 0x7d, 0, 0), // flat_load_dword v3, v[0:1]
      EncodeExp0(0x00, 0x1),
      EncodeExp1(3, 0, 0, 0),
      EncodeSopp(0x01),
  };
  const uint32_t user_data[] = {0x34567000u, 0x00000012u};

  auto options = MakeCompileOptions(ShaderType::Pixel);
  options.user_data = user_data;

  auto result = RecompileForTest(shader, options);
  Check(result.program.info.uses_dma,
        "FLAT user pointer did not enable DMA");
  CheckSpirvBinaryValidates(result.spirv);
}

void TestNewShaderRecompilerFlatAddressDomainsUseDma() {
  const uint32_t segmented_shader[] = {
      EncodeVop2(0x25, 0, 0, 2),
      EncodeVop1(0x01, 1, 1),
      EncodeFlat0(0x0c, 2, 0),
      EncodeFlat1(3, 0x7d, 0, 0), // global_load_dword v3, v[0:1]
      EncodeFlat0(0x1c, 1, 0),
      EncodeFlat1(0, 0x7d, 3, 0), // scratch_store_dword v3, v[0:1]
      0xbf810000u,
  };
  const uint32_t user_data[] = {0x34567000u, 0u, 0x1000u};

  auto options = MakeCompileOptions(ShaderType::Compute);
  options.user_data = user_data;
  ShaderComputeInputInfo compute{};
  compute.scratch_size_dwords = 1;
  options.input_info.compute = &compute;

  auto result = RecompileForTest(segmented_shader, options);
  Check(result.program.info.uses_dma,
        "GLOBAL null-SADDR did not enable DMA");
  Check((result.ir_dump.find("GetScratchResource") != std::string::npos) &&
            result.program.scratch_dwords == 1,
        "SCRATCH incorrectly entered guest address tracking");
#if KYTY_PLATFORM != KYTY_PLATFORM_WINDOWS
  // A local aperture proof must not admit a median which can still produce a
  // canonical global address. Such stores need the existing ownership proof.
  const uint32_t mixed_domain_store[] = {
      EncodeSop1(0x04, 8, 237), // s_mov_b64 s[8:9], private_base
      EncodeVop3Word0(0x159, 1),
      EncodeVop3Word1(128, 9, 256 + 2), // median(0, private high, dynamic v2)
      EncodeFlat0(0x1c, 0, 0), EncodeFlat1(0, 0x7d, 3, 0),
      EncodeSopp(0x01),
  };
  ExpectFatal([&]() { (void)RecompileForTest(mixed_domain_store, options); },
              "mixed local/global FLAT store bypassed GPU ownership tracking");
  const uint32_t changed_mask_store[] = {
      EncodeSop1(0x04, 8, 237), EncodeSop1(0x04, 10, 235),
      EncodeVop1(0x01, 1, 128), // canonical old address high
      EncodeSop1(0x03, 126, 255), 0x55555555u,
      EncodeVop3Word0(0x159, 1), EncodeVop3Word1(9, 11, 256 + 2),
      EncodeSop1(0x04, 126, 193), // restore all lanes after the median
      EncodeFlat0(0x1c, 0, 0), EncodeFlat1(0, 0x7d, 3, 0),
      EncodeSopp(0x01),
  };
  ExpectFatal([&]() { (void)RecompileForTest(changed_mask_store, options); },
              "FLAT proof discarded a differently predicated address value");
#endif
}

void TestCompilerStageInputOwnership() {
  using namespace ShaderRecompiler;
  const uint32_t shader[] = {EncodeSopp(0x01)};
  ShaderVertexInputInfo vertex{};
  vertex.scratch_size_dwords = 3;
  vertex.mesh.scratch_size_dwords = 11;
  vertex.mesh.threads_num[0] = 192;
  vertex.mesh.threads_num[1] = vertex.mesh.threads_num[2] = 1;
  vertex.mesh.primitives_per_group = 62;
  vertex.mesh.vertices_per_group = 64;
  ShaderPixelInputInfo pixel{};
  pixel.scratch_size_dwords = 5;
  ShaderComputeInputInfo compute{};
  compute.scratch_size_dwords = 7;

  for (const auto stage : {ShaderType::Vertex, ShaderType::Pixel,
                           ShaderType::Compute, ShaderType::Mesh}) {
    CompileOptions options{};
    options.stage = stage;
    options.dump_ir = false;
    uint32_t expected_scratch = 0;
    switch (stage) {
    case ShaderType::Vertex:
      options.input_info.vertex = &vertex;
      expected_scratch = 3;
      break;
    case ShaderType::Pixel:
      options.input_info.pixel = &pixel;
      expected_scratch = 5;
      break;
    case ShaderType::Compute:
      options.input_info.compute = &compute;
      expected_scratch = 7;
      break;
    case ShaderType::Mesh:
      options.input_info.vertex = &vertex;
      expected_scratch = 11;
      break;
    default:
      std::abort();
    }
    const auto translated = TranslateProgram(shader, options);
    Check(
        translated.program.scratch_dwords == expected_scratch,
        "translation did not use its stage's authoritative scratch allocation");
  }

  auto options = MakeCompileOptions(ShaderType::Compute);
  options.shader_hash = 0x1234;
  auto translated = TranslateProgram(shader, options);
  options.stage = ShaderType::Unknown;
  options.shader_hash = 0;
  auto compiled = CompileProgram(std::move(translated), options, {});
  Check(compiled.program.stage == ShaderType::Compute &&
            compiled.program.shader_hash == 0x1234,
        "compilation reinterpreted the translated program's identity");
  CheckSpirvBinaryValidates(compiled.spirv);

#if KYTY_PLATFORM != KYTY_PLATFORM_WINDOWS
  const uint32_t auxiliary_position[] = {
      EncodeExp0(0x0d, 0x1), EncodeExp1(0, 0, 0, 0), EncodeSopp(0x01)};
  for (const auto stage : {ShaderType::Pixel, ShaderType::Compute}) {
    ExpectFatal(
        [&] {
          (void)RecompileForTest(auxiliary_position, MakeCompileOptions(stage));
        },
        "auxiliary position export read another stage's input metadata");
  }
  Decoder::Program decoded;
  Decoder::DecodeProgram(shader, decoded);
  const auto cfg = CFG::BuildGraph(decoded);
  Frontend::EmbeddedFetchPlan fetch;
  Frontend::TranslateOptions invalid_fetch{.stage = ShaderType::Compute,
                                           .input_info = {.compute = &compute},
                                           .embedded_fetch = &fetch};
  ExpectFatal(
      [&] { (void)Frontend::TranslateProgram(decoded, cfg, invalid_fetch); },
      "embedded vertex fetch accepted another stage's metadata");
#endif
}

void TestSpirvRepeatedEmission() {
  using namespace ShaderRecompiler;
  const uint32_t shader[] = {EncodeSopp(0x01)};
  ShaderComputeInputInfo compute{};
  compute.threads_num[0] = 64;
  compute.threads_num[1] = compute.threads_num[2] = 1;
  auto options = MakeCompileOptions(ShaderType::Compute);
  options.wave_size = 64;
  options.input_info.compute = &compute;
  auto compiled = RecompileForTest(shader, options);
  IR::IREmitter emitter(compiled.program.blocks.front());
  const auto lane = emitter.Emit(IR::ValueOpcode::LaneId, {});
  const auto value = emitter.Emit(IR::ValueOpcode::IAdd32, {lane, IR::Value(1u)});
  const auto first = emitter.Emit(IR::ValueOpcode::ReadFirstLane,
                                  {value, IR::Value(true)});
  emitter.Emit(IR::ValueOpcode::IAdd32, {first, lane});
  compiled.program.shader_info_complete = false;
  IR::CollectShaderInfo(compiled.program, options.input_info);
  const auto binary = Spirv::EmitProgram(compiled.program, options.input_info);
  CheckSpirvBinaryValidates(binary);
  Check((DisassembleSpirvBinary(binary).find("BuiltIn SubgroupLocalInvocationId") != std::string::npos),
        "collection missed the subgroup requirement of the added IR");
  Check(Spirv::EmitProgram(compiled.program, options.input_info) == binary,
        "repeated emission reused IDs from the previous module");

  compute.host_subgroup_size = 32;
  const auto split = Spirv::EmitProgram(compiled.program, options.input_info);
  CheckSpirvBinaryValidates(split);
  Check(split != binary &&
            Spirv::EmitProgram(compiled.program, options.input_info) == split,
        "split-wave emission did not reset both halves' definitions");

  compute.host_subgroup_size = 64;
  Check(Spirv::EmitProgram(compiled.program, options.input_info) == binary,
        "native-wave re-emission retained split-wave definitions");
  compute.host_subgroup_size = 32;
  Check(Spirv::EmitProgram(compiled.program, options.input_info) == split,
        "split-wave re-emission retained native-wave definitions");
}

void TestSpirvConditionVotes() {
  using namespace ShaderRecompiler;
  using K = CFG::BranchCondition;
  for (const auto [wave, host] : {std::pair{32u, 32u}, std::pair{64u, 64u},
                                  std::pair{64u, 32u}}) {
    const uint32_t shader[] = {EncodeSopp(0x01)};
    ShaderComputeInputInfo compute{};
    compute.wave_size = wave;
    compute.host_subgroup_size = host;
    compute.threads_num[0] = wave;
    compute.threads_num[1] = compute.threads_num[2] = 1;
    auto options = MakeCompileOptions(ShaderType::Compute);
    options.wave_size = wave;
    options.input_info.compute = &compute;
    auto compiled = RecompileForTest(shader, options);
    IR::IREmitter emitter(compiled.program.blocks.front());
    const auto lane = emitter.Emit(IR::ValueOpcode::LaneId, {});
    const auto predicate = emitter.Emit(IR::ValueOpcode::IEqual32, {lane, IR::Value(33u)});
    std::vector<IR::Inst *> references;
    std::vector<IR::Inst *> conditions;
    for (const auto kind : {K::ExecZero, K::VccZero, K::SccZero,
                            K::ExecNonZero, K::VccNonZero, K::SccNonZero}) {
      const auto condition = emitter.Emit(IR::ValueOpcode::ConditionRef, {predicate}, kind);
      conditions.push_back(condition.TryInstruction());
      references.push_back(&compiled.program.blocks.front()->AppendNewInst(
          IR::ValueOpcode::Reference, {condition}));
    }
    const auto scalar = emitter.Emit(IR::ValueOpcode::ConditionRef, {predicate}, K::ScalarInstruction);
    emitter.Emit(IR::ValueOpcode::Reference, {scalar});
    compiled.program.shader_info_complete = false;
    IR::CollectShaderInfo(compiled.program, options.input_info);
    const auto binary = Spirv::EmitProgram(compiled.program, options.input_info);
    CheckSpirvBinaryValidates(binary);
    Check(compiled.program.info.subgroup_vote && !compiled.program.info.subgroup_ballot &&
              SpirvContainsCapability(binary, spv::CapabilityGroupNonUniformVote) &&
              SpirvInstructionOpcodeCount(binary, spv::OpGroupNonUniformAll) == 3 &&
              SpirvInstructionOpcodeCount(binary, spv::OpGroupNonUniformAny) == 3 &&
              SpirvInstructionOpcodeCount(binary, spv::OpGroupNonUniformBallot) == 0,
          "condition votes used ballots, duplicated halves, or lost their capability");
    Check(scalar.TryInstruction()->Definition(0) == predicate.TryInstruction()->Definition(0),
          "scalar instruction condition acquired a subgroup vote");
    if (wave != host) {
      Check(SpirvInstructionOpcodeCount(binary, spv::OpLogicalAnd) == 3 &&
                SpirvInstructionOpcodeCount(binary, spv::OpLogicalOr) == 3 &&
                std::ranges::all_of(conditions, [](const auto *inst) {
                  return inst->Definition(0) == inst->Definition(1);
                }) && scalar.TryInstruction()->Definition(0) == scalar.TryInstruction()->Definition(1),
            "condition votes did not combine and reuse both virtual halves");
    }
    for (auto *reference : references) reference->Invalidate();
    IR::EliminateDeadCode(compiled.program.blocks);
    compiled.program.shader_info_complete = false;
    IR::CollectShaderInfo(compiled.program, options.input_info);
    const auto scalar_only = Spirv::EmitProgram(compiled.program, options.input_info);
    CheckSpirvBinaryValidates(scalar_only);
    Check(!compiled.program.info.subgroup_vote &&
              !SpirvContainsCapability(scalar_only, spv::CapabilityGroupNonUniformVote),
          "recollection retained the removed condition vote capability");
  }
}

void TestRepeatedExportsHaveOneInterface() {
  const uint32_t shader[] = {EncodeExp0(0x0c, 0xf), EncodeExp1(0, 1, 2, 3),
                             EncodeExp0(0x0c, 0xf), EncodeExp1(0, 1, 2, 3),
                             EncodeSopp(0x01)};
  const auto result =
      RecompileForTest(shader, MakeCompileOptions(ShaderType::Vertex));
  Check(result.program.info.outputs.size() == 1,
        "repeated exports duplicated the collected shader interface");
  CheckSpirvBinaryValidates(result.spirv);
  uint32_t outputs = 0;
  for (size_t offset = 5; offset < result.spirv.size();) {
    if ((result.spirv[offset] & spv::OpCodeMask) == spv::OpVariable &&
        result.spirv[offset + 3] == spv::StorageClassOutput) {
      outputs++;
    }
    offset += result.spirv[offset] >> spv::WordCountShift;
  }
  Check(outputs == 2 && SpirvHasDecorationValue(result.spirv, 11u, 3u),
        "repeated exports duplicated Position or its clipping-error plane");
}

void CheckSpirvBlockSourceMapping(TestCompileResult &result) {
  using namespace ShaderRecompiler;
  const auto options = MakeCompileOptions(ShaderType::Compute);
  const auto plain = Spirv::EmitProgram(result.program, options.input_info);
  Check(SpirvInstructionOpcodeCount(plain, spv::OpString) == 0 &&
            SpirvInstructionOpcodeCount(plain, spv::OpLine) == 0 &&
            SpirvInstructionOpcodeCount(plain, spv::OpName) == 0,
        "default emission unexpectedly contains debug info");
  const auto mapped =
      Spirv::EmitProgram(result.program, options.input_info, 0, {}, true);
  Check(SpirvInstructionOpcodeCount(mapped, spv::OpName) != 0,
        "debug emission omitted names");
  CheckSpirvBinaryValidates(mapped);
  uint32_t source = 0;
  uint32_t label = 0;
  size_t lines = 0;
  uint32_t previous = spv::OpNop;
  for (size_t at = 5; at < mapped.size();) {
    const auto op = mapped[at] & spv::OpCodeMask;
    if (op == spv::OpLabel) label = mapped[at + 1];
    if (op == spv::OpString) {
      source = mapped[at + 1];
      Check(std::string(reinterpret_cast<const char *>(&mapped[at + 2]))
                .find("-block-byte-pc-plus-one") != std::string::npos,
            "debug source filename does not identify block offset encoding");
    } else if (op == spv::OpLine) {
      Check(previous == spv::OpLabel && mapped[at + 1] == source &&
                mapped[at + 3] == 0 &&
                std::ranges::any_of(result.program.blocks, [&](const auto *block) {
                  return block->Definition() == label &&
                         mapped[at + 2] == block->start_pc + 1u;
                }),
            "debug source line does not identify a native block after its label");
      ++lines;
    }
    previous = op;
    at += mapped[at] >> spv::WordCountShift;
  }
  Check(source != 0 && lines >= result.program.blocks.size(),
        "debug emission omitted native block source mapping");
  Check(Spirv::EmitProgram(result.program, options.input_info) == plain,
        "debug re-emission changed the default binary");
}

void TestNewShaderRecompilerSpirvSizeBaselines() {
  const auto compile = [](const char *name, std::span<const uint32_t> shader,
                          const SpirvMetrics &budget,
                          ShaderType stage = ShaderType::Compute) {
    auto options = MakeCompileOptions(stage);
    options.dump_ir = true;

    auto result = RecompileForTest(shader, options);
    CheckSpirvBinaryValidates(result.spirv);
    CheckSpirvBudget(name, result.spirv, budget);
    return result;
  };

  const uint32_t empty[] = {EncodeSopp(0x01)};
  const auto empty_result =
      compile("empty", empty,
              {.words = 64, .instructions = 20, .labels = 4, .branches = 3});
  const auto empty_metrics = MeasureSpirv(empty_result.spirv);
  Check(empty_metrics.type_voids == 1u && empty_metrics.type_functions == 1u &&
            empty_metrics.type_bools == 0u && empty_metrics.type_ints == 0u &&
            empty_metrics.type_floats == 0u &&
            empty_metrics.type_vectors == 0u &&
            empty_metrics.type_pointers == 0u,
        "empty shader emitted unused core types or pointers");

  const uint32_t dead_gds[] = {
      EncodeDs0(0x36, 0) | (1u << 17u),
      EncodeDs1(0, 0, 1),
      EncodeSopp(0x01),
  };
  const auto dead_gds_result =
      compile("dead-gds", dead_gds,
              {.words = 64, .instructions = 20, .labels = 4, .branches = 3});
  Check(dead_gds_result.program.bindings.descriptor_counts[static_cast<size_t>(ShaderRecompiler::IR::DescriptorBindingKind::Gds)] == 0,
        "dead GDS load retained a descriptor binding");

  const uint32_t structured_phi[] = {
      EncodeSMovB32(0, 128),       // s0 = 0
      EncodeSopc(0x0a, 0, 129),    // loop: s_cmp_lt_u32 s0, 1
      EncodeSopp(0x04, 2),         // break when scc == 0
      EncodeSop2(0x00, 0, 0, 129), // s_add_u32 s0, s0, 1
      EncodeSopp(0x02, 0xfffcu),   // continue/backedge
      EncodeSopp(0x01),
  };
  auto structured_result = compile("structured-phi", structured_phi,
                                         {.words = 174,
                                          .instructions = 49,
                                          .phis = 1,
                                          .labels = 8,
                                          .loop_merges = 1,
                                          .branches = 6,
                                          .conditional_branches = 1,
                                          .ballots = 2});
  const auto structured_metrics = MeasureSpirv(structured_result.spirv);
  Check((structured_result.ir_dump.find("Phi") != std::string::npos),
        "structured Phi size fixture no longer contains an IR Phi");
  Check(structured_metrics.phis == 1u &&
            structured_metrics.function_variables == 0u &&
            structured_metrics.loads == 0u && structured_metrics.stores == 0u,
        "structured Phi retained a spill variable or edge memory operation");
  CheckSpirvPhiParents(structured_result.spirv);
  CheckSpirvBlockSourceMapping(structured_result);
  const auto structured_repeat =
      compile("structured-phi-repeat", structured_phi,
              {.words = 174,
               .instructions = 49,
               .phis = 1,
               .labels = 8,
               .loop_merges = 1,
               .branches = 6,
               .conditional_branches = 1,
               .ballots = 2});
  Check(structured_repeat.spirv == structured_result.spirv,
        "deferred Phi patching is not deterministic");

  const uint32_t wide_buffer[] = {
      EncodeMubuf0(0x0e, 0),
      EncodeMubuf1(0, 0, 1), // buffer_load_dwordx4 v[0:3]
      EncodeMubuf0(0x1e, 16),
      EncodeMubuf1(0, 0, 1), // buffer_store_dwordx4 v[0:3]
      EncodeSopp(0x01),
  };
  const auto wide_result = compile("wide-buffer", wide_buffer,
                                   {.words = 807,
                                    .instructions = 211,
                                    .runtime_arrays = 1,
                                    .variables = 2,
                                    .loads = 9,
                                    .stores = 4,
                                    .phis = 5,
                                    .labels = 34,
                                    .selection_merges = 10,
                                    .branches = 23,
                                    .conditional_branches = 10});
  Check((wide_result.decoded_dump.find("BUFFER_LOAD_DWORDX4") != std::string::npos),
        "wide buffer size fixture no longer decodes its x4 load");
  Check((wide_result.decoded_dump.find("BUFFER_STORE_DWORDX4") != std::string::npos),
        "wide buffer size fixture no longer decodes its x4 store");
  uint32_t wide_loads = 0;
  uint32_t wide_stores = 0;
  uint32_t scalar_loads = 0;
  uint32_t scalar_stores = 0;
  for (const auto *block : wide_result.program.blocks) {
    for (const auto &inst : *block) {
      switch (inst.GetOpcode()) {
      case ShaderRecompiler::IR::ValueOpcode::LoadBufferU32x4:
        wide_loads++;
        break;
      case ShaderRecompiler::IR::ValueOpcode::StoreBufferU32x4:
        wide_stores++;
        break;
      case ShaderRecompiler::IR::ValueOpcode::LoadBufferU32:
        scalar_loads++;
        break;
      case ShaderRecompiler::IR::ValueOpcode::StoreBufferU32:
        scalar_stores++;
        break;
      default:
        break;
      }
    }
  }
  Check(wide_loads == 1u && wide_stores == 1u && scalar_loads == 0u &&
            scalar_stores == 0u,
        "wide buffer fixture retained scalar sibling memory operations");

  const uint32_t wide_lds[] = {
      EncodeDs0(0xff, 0),  EncodeDs1(0, 0, 4), // ds_read_b128 v[0:3], v4
      EncodeDs0(0xdf, 16), EncodeDs1(0, 0, 4), // ds_write_b128 v[0:3], v4
      EncodeSopp(0x01),
  };
  const auto wide_lds_result = compile("wide-lds", wide_lds,
                                       {.words = 548,
                                        .instructions = 156,
                                        .variables = 1,
                                        .workgroup_variables = 1,
                                        .loads = 4,
                                        .stores = 4,
                                        .phis = 5,
                                        .labels = 34,
                                        .selection_merges = 10,
                                        .branches = 23,
                                        .conditional_branches = 10});
  const auto wide_lds_metrics = MeasureSpirv(wide_lds_result.spirv);
  Check(wide_lds_metrics.workgroup_variables == 1u &&
            wide_lds_metrics.runtime_arrays == 0u &&
            wide_lds_metrics.array_lengths == 0u,
        "native wide LDS fixture emitted the wrong storage topology");

  const uint32_t wide_gds[] = {
      EncodeDs0(0xff, 0) | (1u << 17u),
      EncodeDs1(0, 0, 4),
      EncodeDs0(0xdf, 16) | (1u << 17u),
      EncodeDs1(0, 0, 4),
      EncodeSopp(0x01),
  };
  const auto wide_gds_result = compile("wide-gds", wide_gds,
                                       {.words = 577,
                                        .instructions = 162,
                                        .runtime_arrays = 1,
                                        .variables = 1,
                                        .loads = 4,
                                        .stores = 4,
                                        .array_lengths = 1,
                                        .phis = 5,
                                        .labels = 34,
                                        .selection_merges = 10,
                                        .branches = 23,
                                        .conditional_branches = 10});
  const auto wide_gds_metrics = MeasureSpirv(wide_gds_result.spirv);
  Check(wide_gds_metrics.runtime_arrays == 1u &&
            wide_gds_metrics.workgroup_variables == 0u &&
            wide_gds_metrics.array_lengths == 1u,
        "native wide GDS fixture did not share one entry-dominating length");
  Check(wide_gds_result.program.bindings.descriptor_counts[static_cast<size_t>(ShaderRecompiler::IR::DescriptorBindingKind::Gds)] != 0,
        "live native wide GDS access did not allocate its descriptor binding");
  const auto count_shared = [](const auto &result,
                               ShaderRecompiler::IR::ValueOpcode opcode) {
    uint32_t count = 0;
    for (const auto *block : result.program.blocks) {
      count += std::ranges::count(*block, opcode,
                                  &ShaderRecompiler::IR::Inst::GetOpcode);
    }
    return count;
  };
  for (const auto *result : {&wide_lds_result, &wide_gds_result}) {
    Check(count_shared(*result,
                       ShaderRecompiler::IR::ValueOpcode::LoadSharedU32x4) ==
                  1u &&
              count_shared(
                  *result,
                  ShaderRecompiler::IR::ValueOpcode::WriteSharedU32x4) == 1u &&
              count_shared(*result,
                           ShaderRecompiler::IR::ValueOpcode::LoadSharedU32) ==
                  0u &&
              count_shared(*result,
                           ShaderRecompiler::IR::ValueOpcode::WriteSharedU32) ==
                  0u,
          "native wide shared fixture retained scalar sibling operations");
  }

  const uint32_t wqm[] = {
      EncodeVopc(0xc1, 5 + 256, 8), // v_cmp_lt_u32 vcc, v5, v8
      EncodeSop1(0x0a, 2, 106),     // s_wqm_b64 s[2:3], vcc
      EncodeVop1(0x01, 0, 2),       // v_mov_b32 v0, s2
      EncodeExp0(0x0c, 0x1),
      EncodeExp1(0, 0, 0, 0), // POS0.x
      EncodeSopp(0x01),
  };
  const auto wqm_result = compile("wqm", wqm,
                                  {.words = 407,
                                   .instructions = 99,
                                   .variables = 4,
                                   .loads = 3,
                                   .stores = 2,
                                   .labels = 6,
                                   .selection_merges = 1,
                                   .branches = 4,
                                   .conditional_branches = 1,
                                   .ballots = 1},
                                  ShaderType::Vertex);
  Check((wqm_result.ir_dump.find("WqmU64") != std::string::npos),
        "WQM size fixture no longer reaches scalar mask expansion");

  const uint32_t dispatcher[] = {
      EncodeSopp(0x05, 2),       // entry -> B, fallthrough A
      EncodeSopp(0x02, 0),       // A -> C
      EncodeSopp(0x05, 0xfffeu), // C -> A, fallthrough B
      EncodeSopp(0x02, 0xfffeu), // B -> C
      EncodeSopp(0x01),
  };
  auto dispatcher_result = compile("dispatcher", dispatcher,
                                         {.words = 255,
                                          .instructions = 70,
                                          .variables = 3,
                                          .function_variables = 3,
                                          .loads = 3,
                                          .stores = 6,
                                          .phis = 2,
                                          .labels = 13,
                                          .loop_merges = 1,
                                          .selection_merges = 1,
                                          .branches = 10,
                                          .conditional_branches = 1,
                                          .switches = 1,
                                          .ballots = 1});
  Check(dispatcher_result.program.dispatcher_fallback &&
            (dispatcher_result.ir_dump.find("Phi") != std::string::npos) &&
            SpirvInstructionOpcodeCount(dispatcher_result.spirv, 245u) == 2u &&
            SpirvInstructionOpcodeCount(dispatcher_result.spirv, 251u) == 1u,
        "dispatcher size fixture lost its two control Phis or switch");
  CheckSpirvPhiParents(dispatcher_result.spirv);
  CheckSpirvBlockSourceMapping(dispatcher_result);
}

`tools/pipeline-share-server/README.md`:

```md
# pipeline-share-server

Server that shares the KytyPS5 pipeline manifest (`.kpm`, see
`src/graphics/host_gpu/renderer/pipeline/pipelineManifest.cpp` and `assets/pipelines`) between
users. Emulators that opted in upload the records they discover for the first time and download
the ones they lack, so what some play benefits the others in real time. A record holds only
hashes and pipeline state, never game code.

The server keeps everything in memory, saves it to disk every few minutes and on exit, and
exports each partition as `.kpm` files ready to merge into `assets/pipelines`.

## Seeds: the manifests of the repository

At every start, before listening, the server downloads the `.kpm` files of the repository
(`assets/pipelines` on `main` of `zorde23/kyty-gpu-hybrid`, through the public GitHub API; a file is
only downloaded when its Git blob id changed and its content is checked against it) and keeps a
copy in `<data-dir>/seeds/main/`. Their records are **published** (given a sequence number, in
file order, so modules come before the pipelines that name them) unless already published: the
union of what the players sent and what the repository ships, nothing is ever removed. A record
of the repository that a player uploads is not counted as new, and the export leaves out
everything the repository has (the export is what is new and must go into the repository).
If GitHub cannot be reached (no network, rate limit, 60 s in total) the copy on disk is used,
the log says so and the server starts anyway.

Which clients get what:

- **New clients** (`proto` 2): with a cursor they get every published record after it. A client
  that has just been installed, updated to another release or never reconciled sends, in each
  page of its first round, `have`: the hashes of the records of its `assets/pipelines` file and
  its shared manifest. It then only gets what it does not have (records of other players, and
  what a newer repository ships). When it ends, it goes back to the cursor alone.
- **The first clients** (v19, no `proto` and no `have`): they get what the *default release*
  does not ship (`--default-release v19`). That release is downloaded once from the tag of the
  same name of the repository (immutable; `<data-dir>/seeds/v19/`, marked `.complete`, never asked
  again). Without it they would be sent what they already have.

Flow of a new release: push to `main`, **restart the server before publishing the release** (it
downloads the new manifests and publishes their records), and then publish. The clients of the
new release reconcile with their manifests and receive only what the server has beyond them;
the clients of the old release (and v19) receive what the new release brings through the cursor.
Nothing is copied by hand.

## Build and run

```
cargo build --release
./target/release/pipeline-share-server --data-dir data --listen 127.0.0.1:8787 --quorum 2
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--listen` | `127.0.0.1:8787` | HTTP address (HTTPS goes through a reverse proxy) |
| `--data-dir` | `data` | `state.json`, `export/` and `seeds/` |
| `--seed-repo` / `--seed-ref` / `--seed-path` | `zorde23/kyty-gpu-hybrid` / `main` / `assets/pipelines` | where the seeds are downloaded from at every start |
| `--seed-api` / `--seed-timeout` | `https://api.github.com` / 60 | GitHub API and seconds for all the downloads of a start (then the copies on disk are used) |
| `--no-seed` | off | no download and no copies from `seeds/` (tests, offline) |
| `--default-release` | `default` | release whose records are left out for clients that send neither `proto` nor `have`. If `--known` has no release with that name and it is not `default`, it is downloaded once from the tag of that name (`v19`) |
| `--known <dir>` | none | optional, for tests or without network: every **subfolder** is a release with its `.kpm` files (`<TITLE>_<VERSION>.kpm`, as `assets/pipelines`): `known/v19/`, `known/v20/`. `.kpm` files directly in the folder are the release `default`. Same treatment as the seeds |
| `--quorum` | 2 | distinct clients from distinct IPs needed to publish a record (1 publishes at once) |
| `--save-interval` | 300 | seconds between saves (also on Ctrl-C / SIGTERM) |
| `--real-ip-header` | none | header with the real client IP set by the proxy (`X-Real-IP`). When set it is required (400 without a valid IP) and replaces the TCP peer for quorum, limits and the IP hash. Only use it behind a proxy that overwrites it, with the port not reachable from outside |
| `--ip-requests` / `--ip-window` | 30 / 600 | requests per IP per window (seconds) |
| `--client-daily` / `--ip-daily` | 20000 / 100000 | new records per client / per IP per UTC day |
| `--partition-cap` | 200000 | records (published and pending) per partition |
| `--max-partitions` | 500 | partitions (title and version) accepted |

`RUST_LOG=debug` logs every request (by default only the ones that publish something, saves and
errors). IPs are only kept as salted hashes (the salt lives in `state.json`); client ids too.

## Output

`data/state.json` (written to a temporary file and renamed, loaded at start) and, per format and
partition, in `data/export/v1/` (one folder per format version):

- `<TITLE>_<VERSION>.kpm`: published records in publication order (modules before the
  pipelines that name them), without what the seeds (the repository) already have;
- `<TITLE>_<VERSION>.pending.kpm`: records without quorum yet (or pipelines waiting for modules).

Both start with the format header, so they merge with `assets/pipelines/<TITLE>_<VERSION>.kpm`
by appending the lines that are not there.

## Protocol v1

`GET /v1/health` answers 200 `ok`.

`POST /v1/sync`, JSON body (`Content-Encoding: gzip` accepted), response JSON gzipped when the
client sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip`:

```json
{"client": "<uuid v4>", "emulator": "<free text, <=64>", "format": "# kyty pipeline manifest v1",
 "title": "PPSA21564", "version": "01.007.000", "cursor": 0, "records": ["M ...", "P ...", "T ..."],
 "proto": 2, "have": ["<16 hex digits>", "..."]}
```

`proto` (2 for the clients that reconcile) and `have` are optional. `have` is only sent while the
client reconciles its manifests with the server: the hashes (first 8 bytes of the SHA-256 of the
record line, in hex) of the records it already has, at most `partition_cap` of them (413 beyond).

Response 200: `{"cursor": <u64>, "records": [...], "more": <bool>}`: the published records of the
partition (format, title, version) after `cursor`, in order. At most 20000 published records are
*reviewed* per response, and the ones the client must not get are left out, so a response can
carry fewer records (even none) with `more` set; the cursor stops at the last record reviewed.
While `more` is true the client repeats with the new cursor (and the same `have`). A cursor
beyond what the server has (it lost its state) restarts from 0.

What is left out: with `have`, the records whose hash is in it; with `proto` 2 and no `have`,
nothing; with neither (the first clients), the records of the default release.

Errors: 400 (invalid request, short text; also when every record is garbage), 413 (body over 4 MiB
decompressed or over 5000 records), 429 with `Retry-After` (IP limit, too many partitions).

Validation: `title` `^[A-Z]{4}[0-9]{5}$`; `version` `^[0-9A-Za-z._-]{1,32}$`; `format` starts with
`# kyty pipeline manifest v` and is at most 64 bytes (what follows must be `[0-9A-Za-z._-]+`, it
names the export folder); `client` a UUID v4; each record starts with `M `, `P ` or `T `, only
ASCII 0x20-0x7E, at most 8192 bytes (an `M` has a 12 hex digit id, the `v=`/`h=`/`d=`/`p=` fields of
a `P` hold ids of that form); invalid records are dropped one by one.

Rules: the identity of a record is its exact line. A record is published (given the next
sequence number and served) once `--quorum` distinct clients from distinct IPs sent it. A `P` is
published only when all the modules it names are published (the repository's count); until then
it waits.

Pipelines that no draw creates from the modules they name are never published, as the emulator's
`LoadManifest()` leaves them out (`validate::pipeline_link_error`, the same checks as
`PipelineLinkError()` in `pipelineManifest.cpp`): a VS or mesh stage, or an LS, HS and TES, with an
optional PS; as many vertex attributes as the VS or LS reads (none for a mesh stage), each from a
binding of the pipeline; the LS's patch size, or patches of 3 points for a rectangle list. The
modules are the published `M` records of the same partition (the first one of an id). Recordings
made before the emulator fixed `RecordPipeline()` mixed up the places of their modules and wrote
such pipelines (Elden Ring Nightreign crashed creating one whose vertex stage was a TES). A
pipeline whose modules are all published is checked when it arrives, and one that waits for them
when they are: it is dropped (not the request) and counted in the `sync` log line (`unlinked N`,
with an example). The seeds are checked as they are published (a `seeds <title>_<version>: left
out N pipelines` warning at start), and at every start the server takes out of its state the
pipelines it published or kept before it checked them (`state <title>_<version>: removed ...`):
a published one leaves an empty line in `state.json` (a tombstone, neither served nor exported)
so that the cursors of the clients keep pointing at the same records. When it removes any, it
copies `state.json` to `state.json.before-unlinked-<unix time>` and saves the cleaned state at
once (`state cleaned: N pipelines removed`).
When a client has used up its daily budget the rest of its records are ignored (the response
still carries what it lacks); when the IP budget of requests is used up the answer is 429.

## Deployment (Docker, behind Cloudflare and nginx)

Public URL: `https://kytypipes.mhcruz.com`. Cloudflare ends HTTPS, the nginx container
(`nginx-nginx-1`, network `nginx-net`) only accepts Cloudflare IPs and forwards over HTTP to
`kytypipes-app:8787`. The server does not see the real IP as the TCP peer, hence
`--real-ip-header X-Real-IP` (nginx sets it from `CF-Connecting-IP`). The port is not published
on the host.

Folder on the VPS (Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64, Docker; no Rust needed):

```
/servers/kytypipes/
    src/        this crate (Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, src/, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml)
    data/       state.json, export/ and seeds/   (the container runs as uid 65532)
```

The compose file goes next to `src/` and `data/`, and `.env` tells it where the
sources are (`SRC`, default `.` when it is run from the crate folder). First start:

```
mkdir -p /servers/kytypipes/{src,data}
# copy tools/pipeline-share-server/* (not target/) to /servers/kytypipes/src/
cp /servers/kytypipes/src/docker-compose.yml /servers/kytypipes/
echo 'SRC=./src' > /servers/kytypipes/.env
sudo chown 65532:65532 /servers/kytypipes/data
cd /servers/kytypipes
docker compose build
docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f
```

Update (new server code): copy the new sources over `src/` (and the compose file if it changed), then `docker compose build &&
docker compose up -d`. The container is stopped with SIGTERM and saves its state before exiting
(`stop_grace_period` can be raised for a big state). New repository manifests: push them to
`main` and `docker compose restart` (at every start the server downloads them from GitHub and
publishes their records; pending records that the repository now ships become published, the
published ones stay in the state, and the export leaves out whatever the repository has). The
container needs to reach `api.github.com` and `raw.githubusercontent.com` over HTTPS (the
certificates are embedded in the binary); without them it starts with the copy of `data/seeds/`.
Restart it before publishing the release whose manifests changed.

The state keeps format version 1: the records of the repository are published as any other and
are told apart at run time (the files in `seeds/`), so a state written by an older server loads
unchanged.

Collecting the result: `data/export/v1/*.kpm` are merged into `assets/pipelines` in the repository.

nginx, `/servers/nginx/conf/kytypipes.conf` (same pattern as the other sites of the VPS; reload
nginx afterwards):

```
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name kytypipes.mhcruz.com;
    include /cfips.conf;
    location / {
        resolver 127.0.0.11 ipv6=off;
        set $upstream kytypipes-app;
        proxy_pass http://$upstream:8787;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $http_cf_connecting_ip;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $http_cf_connecting_ip;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto https;
        client_max_body_size 5M;
    }
}
```

Cloudflare: bot mode or security challenges can block requests that do not come from a browser
(the emulator is not one). Exclude `kytypipes.mhcruz.com/v1/*` from challenges (WAF custom rule
with action Skip, or turn off Bot Fight Mode for that host). Test with
`curl https://kytypipes.mhcruz.com/v1/health`, which must answer `ok`.

## Other proxies (Caddy)

Without Cloudflare, Caddy gives HTTPS with a one-line config. `X-Real-IP` is set by Caddy from the
connection, replacing any value the client sends:

```
kytypipes.example.com {
    reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8787 {
        header_up X-Real-IP {remote_host}
    }
}
```

Run the server with `--real-ip-header X-Real-IP`.

state, limits, HTTP with gzip, persistence save/restart/export) and `cargo clippy --all-targets`.

`tools/pipeline-share-server/src/http.rs`:

```rs
//! HTTP layer: `GET /v1/health` and `POST /v1/sync`.

use crate::limits::Limits;
use crate::store::{self, Filter, PartKey, Store};
use crate::validate::{self, MAX_BODY_BYTES, MAX_RECORDS_PER_REQUEST};
use axum::body::{Body, Bytes};
use axum::extract::{ConnectInfo, Request, State};
use axum::http::{header, HeaderMap, HeaderValue, StatusCode};
use axum::middleware::{self, Next};
use axum::response::{IntoResponse, Response};
use axum::routing::{get, post};
use axum::{Extension, Router};
use flate2::read::GzDecoder;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::io::Read;
use std::net::{IpAddr, SocketAddr};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, MutexGuard};
use tower_http::compression::CompressionLayer;

pub struct App {
    pub store: Mutex<Store>,
    pub limits: Mutex<Limits>,
    /// Header with the client IP set by the reverse proxy (e.g. `X-Real-IP`). When set, it is
    /// required and replaces the TCP peer address.
    pub real_ip_header: Option<String>,
    pub clock: Box<dyn Fn() -> u64 + Send + Sync>,
}

impl App {
    pub fn new(store: Store, limits: Limits, real_ip_header: Option<String>) -> Self {
        Self { store: Mutex::new(store), limits: Mutex::new(limits), real_ip_header, clock: Box::new(unix_now) }
    }

    pub fn store(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, Store> {
        self.store.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
    }

    pub fn limits_gc(&self, now: u64) {
        self.limits().gc(now);
    }

    fn limits(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, Limits> {
        self.limits.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
    }
}

pub fn unix_now() -> u64 {
    std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map_or(0, |d| d.as_secs())
}

pub fn router(app: Arc<App>) -> Router {
    Router::new()
        .route("/v1/health", get(|| async { "ok" }))
        .route("/v1/sync", post(sync).route_layer(middleware::from_fn_with_state(app.clone(), rate_limit)))
        .layer(axum::extract::DefaultBodyLimit::max(MAX_BODY_BYTES))
        .layer(CompressionLayer::new().gzip(true))
        .with_state(app)
}

/// Salted hash of the (masked) client address, set by the rate limit for the handler.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct IpHash(u64);

/// The client address: the proxy's header when configured (`None` when it is missing or not an
/// IP), else the TCP peer.
fn client_ip(app: &App, headers: &HeaderMap, peer: Option<IpAddr>) -> Option<IpAddr> {
    match app.real_ip_header.as_deref() {
        Some(name) => headers
            .get(name)
            .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
            // Several values: the last one is the one our own proxy appended.
            .and_then(|v| v.rsplit(',').next())
            .and_then(|v| v.trim().parse::<IpAddr>().ok()),
        None => Some(peer.unwrap_or(IpAddr::from([0, 0, 0, 0]))),
    }
}

/// IPv6 addresses are masked to their /64 and mapped IPv4 ones are IPv4.
fn mask_ip(ip: IpAddr) -> String {
    match ip {
        IpAddr::V4(v4) => v4.to_string(),
        IpAddr::V6(v6) => match v6.to_ipv4_mapped() {
            Some(v4) => v4.to_string(),
            None => {
                let s = v6.segments();
                format!("{:x}:{:x}:{:x}:{:x}", s[0], s[1], s[2], s[3])
            }
        },
    }
}

async fn rate_limit(State(app): State<Arc<App>>, mut req: Request, next: Next) -> Response {
    let peer = req.extensions().get::<ConnectInfo<SocketAddr>>().map(|c| c.0.ip());
    let Some(ip) = client_ip(&app, req.headers(), peer) else {
        return bad("missing or invalid real ip header");
    };
    let ip = mask_ip(ip);
    let hash = app.store().hash("ip", &ip);
    let now = (app.clock)();
    if let Err(retry) = app.limits().check_ip(hash, now) {
        tracing::debug!("429 rate limit for ip hash {hash:016x}");
        return too_many(retry, "too many requests");
    }
    req.extensions_mut().insert(IpHash(hash));
    next.run(req).await
}

fn too_many(retry_after: u64, text: &'static str) -> Response {
    let mut resp = (StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, text).into_response();
    if let Ok(v) = HeaderValue::from_str(&retry_after.to_string()) {
        resp.headers_mut().insert(header::RETRY_AFTER, v);
    }
    resp
}

fn bad(text: &'static str) -> Response {
    (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, text).into_response()
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct SyncRequest {
    client: String,
    emulator: String,
    format: String,
    title: String,
    version: String,
    cursor: u64,
    records: Vec<String>,
    /// Protocol revision of the client. Absent in the first clients (they get what the default
    /// release does not ship); 2 or more answer with everything published unless `have` is set.
    #[serde(default)]
    proto: Option<u32>,
    /// Hashes (first 8 bytes of the SHA-256, 16 hex digits) of the records the client has, sent
    /// while it reconciles its manifests with the server: it only gets what it does not have.
    #[serde(default)]
    have: Option<Vec<String>>,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
struct SyncResponse<'a> {
    cursor: u64,
    records: &'a [Arc<str>],
    more: bool,
}

fn gunzip(data: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Box<Response>> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let limit = MAX_BODY_BYTES as u64 + 1;
    if GzDecoder::new(data).take(limit).read_to_end(&mut out).is_err() {
        return Err(Box::new(bad("invalid gzip body")));
    }
    if out.len() > MAX_BODY_BYTES {
        return Err(Box::new((StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "body too large").into_response()));
    }
    Ok(out)
}

async fn sync(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(IpHash(ip)): Extension<IpHash>,
    headers: HeaderMap,
    body: Bytes,
) -> Response {
    let encoding = headers
        .get(header::CONTENT_ENCODING)
        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
        .map(|v| v.trim().to_ascii_lowercase());
    let body = match encoding.as_deref() {
        None | Some("") | Some("identity") => body.to_vec(),
        Some("gzip") => match gunzip(&body) {
            Ok(b) => b,
            Err(r) => return *r,
        },
        Some(_) => return bad("unsupported content-encoding"),
    };
    let Ok(req) = serde_json::from_slice::<SyncRequest>(&body) else {
        return bad("invalid json");
    };
    if !validate::valid_client(&req.client) {
        return bad("invalid client");
    }
    if !validate::valid_emulator(&req.emulator) {
        return bad("invalid emulator");
    }
    if !validate::valid_format(&req.format) {
        return bad("invalid format");
    }
    if !validate::valid_title(&req.title) {
        return bad("invalid title");
    }
    if !validate::valid_version(&req.version) {
        return bad("invalid version");
    }
    if req.records.len() > MAX_RECORDS_PER_REQUEST {
        return (StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "too many records").into_response();
    }
    let received = req.records.len();
    let mut records = Vec::with_capacity(received);
    for line in req.records {
        if let Some(parsed) = validate::parse_record(&line) {
            records.push((line, parsed));
        }
    }
    if received > 0 && records.is_empty() {
        return bad("no valid records");
    }

    let have_count = req.have.as_ref().map(Vec::len);
    let cap = app.store().settings().partition_cap;
    let filter = match &req.have {
        Some(have) => {
            if have.len() > cap {
                return (StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "too many hashes").into_response();
            }
            Filter::Have(have.iter().filter_map(|h| store::parse_hash(h)).collect())
        }
        None if req.proto.is_some_and(|p| p >= 2) => Filter::None,
        None => Filter::DefaultRelease,
    };

    let key = PartKey::new(&req.format, &req.title, &req.version);
    let now = (app.clock)();
    let mut store = app.store();
    let client = store.hash("client", &req.client);
    let mut limits = app.limits();
    let budget = limits.remaining_new(client, ip, now);
    let outcome = store.submit(&key, client, ip, &records, budget);
    limits.add_new(client, ip, outcome.counted, now);
    drop(limits);
    if outcome.partition_refused {
        return too_many(3600, "too many partitions");
    }
    let (cursor, lines, more) = store.fetch(&key, req.cursor, &filter);
    drop(store);
    let unlinked = outcome.unlinked.count;
    let level =
        if outcome.published > 0 || unlinked > 0 { tracing::Level::INFO } else { tracing::Level::DEBUG };
    let mut msg = format!(
        "sync {}/{} client {:08x} rx {} valid {} new {} published {} dropped {} unlinked {} have {:?} cursor {}->{} tx {} more {}",
        req.title,
        req.version,
        client as u32,
        received,
        records.len(),
        outcome.counted,
        outcome.published,
        outcome.dropped,
        unlinked,
        have_count,
        req.cursor,
        cursor,
        lines.len(),
        more
    );
    // Pipelines that no draw creates from the modules they name are left out one by one.
    if let Some(example) = &outcome.unlinked.example {
        msg += &format!("; unlinked pipelines such as {example}");
    }
    if level == tracing::Level::INFO {
        tracing::info!("{msg}");
    } else {
        tracing::debug!("{msg}");
    }
    let json = match serde_json::to_vec(&SyncResponse { cursor, records: &lines, more }) {
        Ok(j) => j,
        Err(_) => return (StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "encoding error").into_response(),
    };
    let mut resp = Response::new(Body::from(json));
    resp.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, HeaderValue::from_static("application/json"));
    resp
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::limits::LimitConfig;
    use crate::store::Settings;
    use flate2::write::GzEncoder;
    use flate2::Compression;
    use http_body_util::BodyExt;
    use std::io::Write;
    use tower::ServiceExt;

    const FMT: &str = "# kyty pipeline manifest v1";
    const M1: &str = "M 000000000001 vs code=aa";
    const P1: &str = "P v=000000000001";
    const CLIENT_A: &str = "0b1c2d3e-4f50-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d";
    const CLIENT_B: &str = "1b1c2d3e-4f50-4a6b-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d";

    fn app(quorum: usize, ip_requests: u32) -> Arc<App> {
        let store = Store::with_salt(Settings { quorum, ..Default::default() }, [1; 16]);
        let limits = Limits::new(LimitConfig { ip_requests, ..Default::default() });
        Arc::new(App::new(store, limits, Some("x-real-ip".into())))
    }

    fn body(client: &str, title: &str, cursor: u64, records: &[&str]) -> String {
        serde_json::json!({
            "client": client, "emulator": "kyty test", "format": FMT, "title": title,
            "version": "01.007.000", "cursor": cursor, "records": records,
        })
        .to_string()
    }

    async fn call(
        app: &Arc<App>,
        ip: &str,
        body: Vec<u8>,
        gzip_in: bool,
        gzip_out: bool,
    ) -> (StatusCode, HeaderMap, Vec<u8>) {
        let mut b = Request::builder().method("POST").uri("/v1/sync").header("x-real-ip", ip);
        if gzip_in {
            b = b.header("content-encoding", "gzip");
        }
        if gzip_out {
            b = b.header("accept-encoding", "gzip");
        }
        let resp = router(app.clone()).oneshot(b.body(Body::from(body)).unwrap()).await.unwrap();
        let (parts, body) = resp.into_parts();
        let bytes = body.collect().await.unwrap().to_bytes().to_vec();
        (parts.status, parts.headers, bytes)
    }

    fn gz(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut e = GzEncoder::new(Vec::new(), Compression::default());
        e.write_all(data).unwrap();
        e.finish().unwrap()
    }

    fn json(bytes: &[u8]) -> serde_json::Value {
        serde_json::from_slice(bytes).unwrap()
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn health() {
        let resp = router(app(1, 10))
            .oneshot(Request::get("/v1/health").body(Body::empty()).unwrap())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(resp.status(), StatusCode::OK);
        let bytes = resp.into_body().collect().await.unwrap().to_bytes();
        assert_eq!(&bytes[..], b"ok");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn two_clients_share_through_quorum_with_gzip() {
        let app = app(2, 10);
        // Client A uploads gzip and gets nothing: no quorum yet.
        let (st, _, out) = call(&app, "1.1.1.1", gz(body(CLIENT_A, "PPSA21564", 0, &[M1, P1]).as_bytes()), true, false).await;
        assert_eq!(st, StatusCode::OK);
        assert_eq!(json(&out), serde_json::json!({"cursor": 0, "records": [], "more": false}));
        // Client B from another IP confirms them and receives them, gzipped.
        let (st, headers, out) = call(&app, "2.2.2.2", body(CLIENT_B, "PPSA21564", 0, &[M1, P1]).into_bytes(), false, true).await;
        assert_eq!(st, StatusCode::OK);
        assert_eq!(headers.get("content-encoding").unwrap(), "gzip");
        let mut text = String::new();
        GzDecoder::new(&out[..]).read_to_string(&mut text).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(json(text.as_bytes()), serde_json::json!({"cursor": 2, "records": [M1, P1], "more": false}));
        // Client A polls with its cursor and with an empty list.
        let (_, _, out) = call(&app, "1.1.1.1", body(CLIENT_A, "PPSA21564", 0, &[]).into_bytes(), false, false).await;
        assert_eq!(json(&out)["records"].as_array().unwrap().len(), 2);
        let (_, _, out) = call(&app, "1.1.1.1", body(CLIENT_A, "PPSA21564", 2, &[]).into_bytes(), false, false).await;
        assert_eq!(json(&out), serde_json::json!({"cursor": 2, "records": [], "more": false}));
        // Another partition is empty.
        let (_, _, out) = call(&app, "1.1.1.1", body(CLIENT_A, "PPSA21565", 0, &[]).into_bytes(), false, false).await;
        assert_eq!(json(&out)["records"].as_array().unwrap().len(), 0);
    }

    const M2: &str = "M 000000000002 ps code=bb";

    fn seeded_app() -> Arc<App> {
        use crate::store::{Known, Release};
        let a = app(1, 100);
        let key = PartKey::new(FMT, "PPSA21564", "01.007.000");
        let mut v19 = Known::default();
        v19.add(M1);
        let mut v20 = Known::default();
        v20.add(M1);
        v20.add(M2);
        let release = |name: &str, k: Known| Release {
            name: name.into(),
            parts: std::collections::HashMap::from([(key.clone(), k)]),
        };
        {
            let mut store = a.store();
            store.settings_mut().default_release = "v19".into();
            store.set_known(vec![release("v19", v19), release("v20", v20)]);
        }
        a
    }

    fn records_of(out: &[u8]) -> Vec<String> {
        json(out)["records"].as_array().unwrap().iter().map(|v| v.as_str().unwrap().to_string()).collect()
    }

    fn with(extra: serde_json::Value) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&body(CLIENT_A, "PPSA21564", 0, &[])).unwrap();
        for (k, x) in extra.as_object().unwrap() {
            v[k] = x.clone();
        }
        v.to_string().into_bytes()
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn clients_without_proto_do_not_get_the_default_release() {
        let app = seeded_app();
        // The first clients send neither `proto` nor `have`: what v19 ships is left out.
        let (st, _, out) = call(&app, "1.1.1.1", body(CLIENT_A, "PPSA21564", 0, &[]).into_bytes(), false, false).await;
        assert_eq!(st, StatusCode::OK);
        assert_eq!(records_of(&out), [M2]);
        assert_eq!(json(&out)["cursor"], 2);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn new_clients_get_everything_or_what_they_lack() {
        let app = seeded_app();
        // proto 2 without `have`: normal mode, no filter.
        let (_, _, out) = call(&app, "1.1.1.1", with(serde_json::json!({"proto": 2})), false, false).await;
        assert_eq!(records_of(&out), [M1, M2]);
        // With `have` (reconciliation): only what is not in it; an empty list gets everything.
        let have = format!("{:016x}", crate::store::record_hash(M1));
        let (_, _, out) = call(&app, "1.1.1.1", with(serde_json::json!({"proto": 2, "have": [have, "zz", "12"]})), false, false).await;
        assert_eq!(records_of(&out), [M2]);
        let (_, _, out) = call(&app, "1.1.1.1", with(serde_json::json!({"proto": 2, "have": []})), false, false).await;
        assert_eq!(records_of(&out), [M1, M2]);
        // `have` also wins over the missing proto.
        let (_, _, out) = call(&app, "1.1.1.1", with(serde_json::json!({"have": [have]})), false, false).await;
        assert_eq!(records_of(&out), [M2]);
        // More hashes than a partition may hold: 413.
        let many = vec!["0000000000000000"; 200_001];
        let (st, _, _) = call(&app, "1.1.1.1", with(serde_json::json!({"proto": 2, "have": many})), false, false).await;
        assert_eq!(st, StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn invalid_requests() {
        let app = app(1, 100);
        let ok = |t: &str| body(CLIENT_A, t, 0, &[M1]).into_bytes();
        assert_eq!(call(&app, "1.1.1.1", ok("ppsa21564"), false, false).await.0, StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
        assert_eq!(call(&app, "1.1.1.1", b"{".to_vec(), false, false).await.0, StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
        assert_eq!(call(&app, "1.1.1.1", body("nope", "PPSA21564", 0, &[M1]).into_bytes(), false, false).await.0, StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
        assert_eq!(call(&app, "1.1.1.1", b"not gzip".to_vec(), true, false).await.0, StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
        // Everything is garbage: 400. Some garbage among good records: dropped one by one.
        assert_eq!(call(&app, "1.1.1.1", body(CLIENT_A, "PPSA21564", 0, &["X 1", "M zz"]).into_bytes(), false, false).await.0, StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
        let (st, _, out) = call(&app, "1.1.1.1", body(CLIENT_A, "PPSA21564", 0, &["X 1", M1]).into_bytes(), false, false).await;
        assert_eq!(st, StatusCode::OK);
        assert_eq!(json(&out)["records"], serde_json::json!([M1]));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn too_large() {
        let app = app(1, 100);
        let many = vec![M1; MAX_RECORDS_PER_REQUEST + 1];
        let (st, _, _) = call(&app, "1.1.1.1", body(CLIENT_A, "PPSA21564", 0, &many).into_bytes(), false, false).await;
        assert_eq!(st, StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE);
        let big = vec![b' '; MAX_BODY_BYTES + 1];
        let (st, _, _) = call(&app, "1.1.1.1", big.clone(), false, false).await;
        assert_eq!(st, StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE);
        // A small gzip that inflates beyond the limit.
        let (st, _, _) = call(&app, "1.1.1.1", gz(&big), true, false).await;
        assert_eq!(st, StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn rate_limit_by_ip() {
        let app = app(1, 2);
        for _ in 0..2 {
            let (st, _, _) = call(&app, "9.9.9.9", body(CLIENT_A, "PPSA21564", 0, &[]).into_bytes(), false, false).await;
            assert_eq!(st, StatusCode::OK);
        }
        let (st, headers, _) = call(&app, "9.9.9.9", body(CLIENT_A, "PPSA21564", 0, &[]).into_bytes(), false, false).await;
        assert_eq!(st, StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS);
        assert!(headers.get("retry-after").unwrap().to_str().unwrap().parse::<u64>().unwrap() > 0);
        // Another IP is not affected.
        let (st, _, _) = call(&app, "8.8.8.8", body(CLIENT_A, "PPSA21564", 0, &[]).into_bytes(), false, false).await;
        assert_eq!(st, StatusCode::OK);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn real_ip_header_is_required_when_configured() {
        let app = app(1, 10);
        let req = Request::builder()
            .method("POST")
            .uri("/v1/sync")
            .body(Body::from(body(CLIENT_A, "PPSA21564", 0, &[])))
            .unwrap();
        let resp = router(app.clone()).oneshot(req).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(resp.status(), StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
        assert_eq!(call(&app, "not-an-ip", body(CLIENT_A, "PPSA21564", 0, &[]).into_bytes(), false, false).await.0, StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
    }

    #[test]
    fn ip_masking() {
        assert_eq!(mask_ip("1.2.3.4".parse().unwrap()), "1.2.3.4");
        assert_eq!(mask_ip("::ffff:1.2.3.4".parse().unwrap()), "1.2.3.4");
        assert_eq!(mask_ip("2001:db8:1:2:3:4:5:6".parse().unwrap()), mask_ip("2001:db8:1:2::9".parse().unwrap()));
    }
}

```rs
//! Rate limits. Everything is keyed by salted hashes, never by clear IPs.

use std::collections::HashMap;

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct LimitConfig {
    /// Requests per IP in each window.
    pub ip_requests: u32,
    pub ip_window_secs: u64,
    /// New records per client and per IP per UTC day.
    pub client_daily: u64,
    pub ip_daily: u64,
}

impl Default for LimitConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self { ip_requests: 60, ip_window_secs: 600, client_daily: 20_000, ip_daily: 100_000 }
    }
}

const DAY: u64 = 86_400;

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Limits {
    cfg: LimitConfig,
    ip_req: HashMap<u64, (u64, u32)>,
    client_daily: HashMap<u64, (u64, u64)>,
    ip_daily: HashMap<u64, (u64, u64)>,
}

impl Limits {
    pub fn new(cfg: LimitConfig) -> Self {
        Self { cfg, ..Self::default() }
    }

    /// Counts a request of `ip`; `Err(seconds)` is the `Retry-After` when it is over the limit.
    pub fn check_ip(&mut self, ip: u64, now: u64) -> Result<(), u64> {
        let window = self.cfg.ip_window_secs;
        let entry = self.ip_req.entry(ip).or_insert((now, 0));
        if now >= entry.0 + window {
            *entry = (now, 0);
        }
        if entry.1 >= self.cfg.ip_requests {
            return Err((entry.0 + window).saturating_sub(now).max(1));
        }
        entry.1 += 1;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn used(map: &HashMap<u64, (u64, u64)>, key: u64, now: u64) -> u64 {
        match map.get(&key) {
            Some((day, n)) if *day == now / DAY => *n,
            _ => 0,
        }
    }

    /// How many new records this client from this IP may still add today.
    pub fn remaining_new(&self, client: u64, ip: u64, now: u64) -> u64 {
        let by_client = self.cfg.client_daily.saturating_sub(Self::used(&self.client_daily, client, now));
        let by_ip = self.cfg.ip_daily.saturating_sub(Self::used(&self.ip_daily, ip, now));
        by_client.min(by_ip)
    }

    pub fn add_new(&mut self, client: u64, ip: u64, n: u64, now: u64) {
        let day = now / DAY;
        for (map, key) in [(&mut self.client_daily, client), (&mut self.ip_daily, ip)] {
            let entry = map.entry(key).or_insert((day, 0));
            if entry.0 != day {
                *entry = (day, 0);
            }
            entry.1 += n;
        }
    }

    /// Seconds to the next UTC day, when the daily counters restart.
    pub fn secs_to_next_day(now: u64) -> u64 {
        DAY - now % DAY
    }

    /// Drops the expired entries.
    pub fn gc(&mut self, now: u64) {
        let window = self.cfg.ip_window_secs;
        self.ip_req.retain(|_, (start, _)| now < *start + window);
        let day = now / DAY;
        self.client_daily.retain(|_, (d, _)| *d == day);
        self.ip_daily.retain(|_, (d, _)| *d == day);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn ip_window() {
        let mut l = Limits::new(LimitConfig { ip_requests: 3, ip_window_secs: 100, ..Default::default() });
        for _ in 0..3 {
            assert!(l.check_ip(1, 1000).is_ok());
        }
        assert_eq!(l.check_ip(1, 1040), Err(60));
        assert!(l.check_ip(2, 1040).is_ok(), "another IP is independent");
        assert!(l.check_ip(1, 1100).is_ok(), "the window restarted");
        l.gc(5000);
        assert!(l.ip_req.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn daily_records() {
        let mut l = Limits::new(LimitConfig { client_daily: 10, ip_daily: 15, ..Default::default() });
        let t = 3 * DAY + 5;
        assert_eq!(l.remaining_new(1, 7, t), 10);
        l.add_new(1, 7, 8, t);
        assert_eq!(l.remaining_new(1, 7, t), 2);
        assert_eq!(l.remaining_new(2, 7, t), 7, "the IP limit is shared by clients");
        assert_eq!(l.remaining_new(1, 7, t + DAY), 10, "next day");
        assert_eq!(Limits::secs_to_next_day(t), DAY - 5);
    }
}
